title: Tensor squares for open base change and the clopen comparison
statement:
Let $A,B,C,D$ be schemes and $k:A\hookrightarrow B$, $i:C\hookrightarrow D$ quasi-compact open immersions, $r:A\to C$, $p:B\to D$ proper, with $pk=ir$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $B_C=B\times_D C$, with $b:B_C\to B$, $q:B_C\to C$, and $s=(k,r):A\to B_C$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Work either on their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], or on their vertical sequence sites with sheaves of commutative rings (strict semilinear module systems) [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Choose a ring sheaf $O_D$, a ring sheaf $O_B$ and a structural map $p^{-1}O_D\to O_B$; use $O_C=i^{-1}O_D$, $O_{B_C}=b^{-1}O_B$, $O_A=k^{-1}O_B$ and the induced structural maps. In the sequence case these are ring systems and compatible structural maps, with arbitrary coefficient transitions. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves, $P_h=Lh^*$, canonical tensor comparison $\mu_h:P_h(F\otimes^LG)\cong P_hF\otimes^LP_hG$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and exact open extensions. For any open $j$, let $\delta_j(U,V):j_!U\otimes^LV\cong j_!(U\otimes^LP_jV)$ and the open base-change map $\beta:P_pi_!\cong b_!P_q$ have the open-unit normalization of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The clopen immersion $s$ and projection $\rho_s:F\to s_!P_sF$, identity on $s(A)$ and zero on its complementary open, are as in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Set $\alpha=b_!(\rho_sP_q)\beta$, followed by $b_!s_!\cong k_!$ and $P_sP_q\cong P_r$.
For arbitrary $H\in D(O_C)$ and $N\in D(O_D)$ put $X=P_iN$, $Y=P_pN$, $T=P_rX=P_kY$, using the canonical ringed pullback identifications. The following three equalities hold naturally in the derived categories themselves:
(1) $b_!(\mu_q)\beta_{H\otimes^LX}P_p(\delta_i)=\delta_b(\beta_H\otimes1_Y)\mu_p$, with $P_qX=P_bY$; both sides have source $P_p(i_!H\otimes^LN)$ and target $b_!(P_qH\otimes^LP_bY)$.
(2) For arbitrary $F\in D(O_{B_C})$, $V\in D(O_{B_C})$ one has $s_!(\mu_s)\rho_{s,F\otimes^LV}=\delta_s(\rho_{s,F}\otimes1_V)$. Under the canonical compositors the composite open tensor comparison for $b,s$ equals $\delta_k$.
(3) Consequently the full comparison satisfies
$$k_!(\mu_r)\alpha_{H\otimes^LX}P_p(\delta_i)=\delta_k(\alpha_H\otimes1_Y)\mu_p,$$
as maps $P_p(i_!H\otimes^LN)\to k_!(P_rH\otimes^LT)$. All equations use the specified tensor/pullback compositors and hold also on the ringed sequence sites before evaluation. There is no boundedness, flatness, constructibility or Tor-amplitude condition on $H,N,F,V$; no proper projection isomorphism is assumed.
